name: ICL3232IBNZ-T
title: ICL3221, ICL3222, ICL3223, ICL3232, ICL3241, ICL3243: 3 V to 5.5 V, 250 kbps RS-232 transceivers with 1 µA powerdown
summary: A family of RS-232 drivers and receivers that run from a single 3.0 V to 5.5 V supply and meet EIA/TIA-232 and V.28/V.24 even at 3.0 V. An on-chip regulated doubler and inverter with four 0.1 µF capacitors make ±5.5 V rails; the drivers swing ±5 V minimum into 3 kΩ and run at 250 kbps or more. The ICL3232 (two drivers, two receivers) is always on; the other members add receiver enable, manual shutdown or automatic powerdown that drops the supply to 1 µA when no valid RS-232 level is present, and the ICL3241/43 add three-driver, five-receiver ports with always-on monitor receivers. RS-232 pins are protected to ±15 kV human body model.

circuits.title: ICL3221 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: One driver and one receiver from 3.3 V. C1 and C2 are the flying capacitors of the doubler and the inverter, C3 and C4 hold V+ and V-, and C5 bypasses the 3.3 V supply; all five are 0.1 µF, polarised. EN is grounded so the receiver output is always enabled, FORCEON is grounded and FORCEOFF tied to VCC so automatic powerdown is in charge, and INVALID goes out to the system's power control logic.
notes: C3's negative end may go to VCC instead of ground.

circuits.title: ICL3222 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: Two drivers and two receivers from 3.3 V, pinned as the 18-lead SOIC. C1 and C2 are the flying capacitors of the doubler and the inverter, C3 and C4 hold V+ and V-, and C5 bypasses the 3.3 V supply; all five are 0.1 µF, polarised. EN is grounded so both receiver outputs are enabled and SHDN is tied to VCC so the part never shuts down.
notes: C3's negative end may go to VCC instead of ground.

circuits.title: ICL3223 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: Two drivers and two receivers from 3.3 V with automatic powerdown. C1 and C2 are the flying capacitors of the doubler and the inverter, C3 and C4 hold V+ and V-, and C5 bypasses the 3.3 V supply; all five are 0.1 µF, polarised. EN is grounded, FORCEON is grounded and FORCEOFF tied to VCC so the part sleeps by itself when no valid RS-232 level reaches a receiver; INVALID goes out to the power control logic.

circuits.title: ICL3232 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: Two drivers and two receivers from 3.3 V with no control pins: the part is always on. C1 and C2 are the flying capacitors of the doubler and the inverter, C3 and C4 hold V+ and V-, and C5 bypasses the 3.3 V supply; all five are 0.1 µF, polarised.
notes: C3's negative end may go to VCC instead of ground.

circuits.title: ICL3241 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: A full serial port: three drivers and five receivers from 3.3 V. C1 and C2 are the flying capacitors of the doubler and the inverter, C3 and C4 hold V+ and V-, and C5 bypasses the 3.3 V supply; all five are 0.1 µF, polarised. EN is grounded and SHDN tied to VCC; R1OUTB and R2OUTB give always-on noninverted copies of receivers 1 and 2.

circuits.title: ICL3243 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: Three drivers and five receivers from 3.3 V with automatic powerdown. C1 and C2 are the flying capacitors of the doubler and the inverter, C3 and C4 hold V+ and V-, and C5 bypasses the 3.3 V supply; all five are 0.1 µF, polarised. FORCEON is grounded and FORCEOFF tied to VCC; INVALID goes out to the power control logic and R2OUTB is an always-on noninverted copy of receiver 2.

circuits.title: Manual powerdown with INVALID read back
circuits.description: FORCEOFF and FORCEON are tied together and driven from one power-management line, so automatic powerdown is off and that line becomes a plain shutdown input; INVALID is fed back to the power management logic so it knows when the line carries no valid RS-232 level. The drivers and receivers connect to a UART as usual.
notes: The same connection applies to the ICL3223 and ICL3243.
The rest of the device is wired as in its typical operating circuit.

circuits.title: Holding off automatic powerdown for 100 ms after a forced power-up
circuits.description: The master powerdown line drives FORCEOFF directly and FORCEON through a 0.1 µF capacitor, with 1 MΩ from FORCEON to ground. When the line goes high the capacitor lifts FORCEON with it, which keeps the part on while the RC decays, about 100 ms; after that FORCEON is low and automatic powerdown is back in charge. This gives a slow peripheral time to bring its RS-232 levels up.
notes: The same connection applies to the ICL3223 and ICL3243.
The rest of the device is wired as in its typical operating circuit.

circuits.title: Transmitter loopback test circuit
circuits.description: Each transmitter output drives its own receiver input, loaded with 1000 pF to ground, while a square wave goes into the transmitter input and the receiver output is watched. The charge pump uses the usual four capacitors and the supply is bypassed with 0.1 µF; EN is grounded and SHDN (FORCEOFF on parts that have it) is tied to VCC.
notes: At 120 kbps all transmitters switch at once, each into an RS-232 receiver load in parallel with 1000 pF; at 250 kbps one transmitter switches into 1000 pF and an RS-232 load, the idle ones each driving a receiver input.

operation.text: Six RS-232 transceivers sharing one design: the ICL3221 has one driver and one receiver, the ICL3222, ICL3223 and ICL3232 two of each, and the ICL3241 and ICL3243 three drivers and five receivers with extra always-on monitor receivers. All run from 3.0 V to 5.5 V and meet EIA/TIA-232 and V.28/V.24 at VCC = 3.0 V, with RS-232-compatible levels down to 2.7 V. They are drop-in replacements for the MAX3221, MAX3222, MAX3223, MAX3232, MAX3241, MAX3243 and SP3243; the ICL3221 also upgrades the 5 V MAX221, the ICL3222 the 5 V MAX242 and SP312A, and the ICL3232 the HIN232/ICL232. The parts are latch-up free.

Two regulated charge pumps, a doubler and an inverter, make the ±5.5 V transmitter rails from VCC as low as 3.0 V, so the outputs stay RS-232 compliant across a 3.3 V ±10% supply. At 3.3 V they need only four 0.1 µF capacitors. The pumps run in bursts, stopping once V+ and V- reach their nominal levels, which saves power.

The rail limits of +7 V and -7 V hold for VCC between 3.0 V and 3.6 V. With VCC at 4.5 V to 5.5 V, V+ and V- can approach +9 V and -7 V (the V+ and V- tables give measured values). V+ and V- were tested for breakdown at ±13 V; the measured withstand is ±13 V from either rail to ground and 20 V from V+ to V-. The characterisation covered 3.0 V to 3.6 V fully and 4.5 V to 5.5 V at critical points, with static logic loads.

The transmitters are low-dropout inverting drivers from TTL/CMOS levels to RS-232 levels, powered from the on-chip ±5.5 V rails. On every part except the ICL3232 the outputs go to high impedance in powerdown and can then be pulled to ±12 V. Each part runs at 250 kbps or more with one transmitter driving 3 kΩ and 1000 pF from VCC of 3.0 V or more; with VCC ≥ 3.3 V, 3 kΩ and 250 pF, one transmitter runs at 900 kbps. An open transmitter input floats and can raise the supply current, so unused inputs go to ground.

The standard receivers invert and can be put in three-state by EN or FORCEOFF (not on the ICL3232). The ICL3241 and ICL3243 add noninverting monitor receivers (ROUTB) that stay active whatever the control pins do. Every receiver takes ±25 V at its input and presents 3 kΩ to 7 kΩ even with VCC = 0 V. The Schmitt-trigger input has hysteresis against noise and slow edges.

On the ICL3221, ICL3222, ICL3223 and ICL3241 the inverting receivers are disabled only by EN high. The ICL3243 receivers turn off in forced powerdown but stay on in automatic powerdown. A receiver output driving a powered-down peripheral pushes current through that peripheral's protection diode, so it should be disabled; a disabled receiver cannot wake the system, but on the ICL324X the monitor receiver can, for example for a ring indicator.

In normal operation the supply current is 0.3 mA nominal, even at VCC = 5.5 V. In powerdown it falls to 1 µA: the charge pump stops, V+ falls to VCC and V- to ground, and the transmitter outputs go to three-state. Whether the inverting receivers also turn off depends on the part (truth table).

The ICL3222 and ICL3241 have a SHDN pin: high for normal operation, low for powerdown. Tie it to VCC if shutdown is not wanted. The receiver outputs stay enabled in shutdown; for the lowest current drive EN high as well.

operation.topic: Manual powerdown, FORCEON and FORCEOFF parts
operation.text: The ICL3221, ICL3223 and ICL3243 use two pins. Both high keeps the part always on. FORCEOFF overrides FORCEON, so software toggles FORCEOFF alone to move the part in and out of powerdown; to keep automatic powerdown out of the way entirely, hold FORCEON high. The ICL3243 standard receivers also turn off in manual powerdown, which removes the current path into a shut-down peripheral.

INVALID tells whether any receiver input carries a valid RS-232 level. With the cable unplugged the inputs are pulled to ground by the internal receiver resistors, INVALID goes low and power-management logic can shut the interface down; plugging back in restores valid levels, INVALID goes high and the interface wakes. INVALID can also report DTR or ring indicate, provided every other receiver input is open or grounded. Tying FORCEOFF and FORCEON together turns off automatic powerdown and makes the pair a manual shutdown input.

Leaving powerdown and starting to transmit takes 100 µs under any of the control schemes. With automatic powerdown on, the part goes back to sleep if valid receiver levels do not return within 30 µs of power-up, which a slow peripheral such as a mouse may not manage; an RC on FORCEON (circuit wake-hold) holds automatic powerdown off for 100 ms after a forced power-up.

On the ICL3221, ICL3223 and ICL3243, once 30 µs pass with no valid RS-232 level on any receiver input, the pump and the drivers turn off and the supply falls to 1 µA. This happens when the far end powers off or the cable is removed, and the part wakes when a valid level appears on any receiver input. A level beyond ±2.7 V is valid and keeps the part active; within ±0.3 V is invalid and leads to powerdown; between 0.3 V and 2.7 V in either polarity the outcome is not defined. Automatic powerdown acts when FORCEON is low and FORCEOFF high; FORCEON high disables it, and FORCEOFF low always forces powerdown. INVALID goes low after invalid levels have lasted 30 µs on all receiver inputs and high 1 µs after a valid level; when automatic powerdown is in use, INVALID low means the part is asleep. Recovery from automatic powerdown takes about 100 µs.

The ICL3221, ICL3222, ICL3223 and ICL3241 have an EN input. EN high puts all inverting receiver outputs in high impedance, which keeps a receiver output from feeding current into the input protection diode of a peripheral whose supply is off. EN does not affect the transmitters or the ROUTB outputs.

At 3.3 V the pumps need 0.1 µF capacitors; other supply ranges use the values in the capacitor table, and smaller values are not allowed. Twice the listed capacitance gives less output ripple and a little less power. C2, C3 and C4 may be raised alone, but C1 may only be raised together with them, keeping the ratio of C1 to the others. At the minimum values, make sure capacitance does not fall too far with temperature, or use larger parts. Capacitor ESR tends to climb at low temperature, which raises the rail ripple.
Most designs need only 0.1 µF of supply bypass. Where supply noise matters, bypass VCC to ground with the same value as C1. Place it as close to the IC as possible.
Down to VCC = 2.7 V the transmitter outputs still meet RS-562 levels (±3.7 V) at the full data rate, which normally works with RS-232 receivers.

When the part leaves powerdown the transmitter outputs move cleanly to opposite RS-232 levels without glitches or ringing (each loaded with 3 kΩ and 2500 pF). The transmitters switch on only once the rails exceed about 3 V in magnitude.

The ICL324X can power a serial mouse from a low supply. The regulated pump keeps at least ±5 V on the transmitters in the worst case: 15 mA from the two paralleled V+ transmitters and 7.3 mA from the single V- transmitter. A mouse defeats automatic powerdown, so with one attached both FORCEON and FORCEOFF are tied to VCC.

The transmitters hold the ±5 V RS-232 minimum at high data rates: in the loopback test all transmitters together run at 120 kbps into RS-232 loads with 1000 pF, and a single transmitter runs at 250 kbps into 1000 pF and an RS-232 load.

The parts connect directly to 5 V CMOS and TTL logic. With the part at 3.3 V and the logic at 5 V, the ICL32xx inputs accept AC, HC and CD4000 outputs, but the ICL32xx outputs do not reach those families' VIH (logic compatibility table).

The ICL3221, ICL3222 and ICL3232 fit the pinouts of older 5 V RS-232 transceivers and draw less current over a wider supply range. They work in most 5 V sockets provided ±5 V output swing is enough and no transmitter input pull-ups are needed. In a 5 V replacement C3 may return to VCC; returning it to ground gives slightly better performance.
